I’ve got this little PDP 8 simulator that’s sitting on my cabinet and I wrote a nice little blinking light program in PDP 8 assembly language. Sometimes during a thunderstorm we’ll get a power glitch and the PDP 8 will shut down. Then I have to manually SSH into the raspberry pie and restart it. That’s a pain.

So I had one of my agents write a little script that would restart it for me. The script runs on my laptop, so it has access to my local network. And then I had my @grokbot run that little script every morning, on my laptop,  so that when I wake up in the morning after a thunderstorm, my PDP 8 Blinky Box will still be running.

I love @grokbot.

results.text:
When you have an agent do a lot of work for you in one session while you are AFK.  It is wise to ask the agent to audit that work once you return.  It will likely come up with a longish list of gaps that it could not resolve.  

Have the agent put those gaps into a file before you start working on them.  You don't want them to get lost in context compressions.  

I keep a file named issues.md.  I have the agent put the gaps in that file.  Then, one by one, we analyze the gaps and replace them with true issues to be repaired.  

Finally, I tell it to fix the issues.  And then the cycle repeats.

results.text:
The deeper you go with the agents, the more they invent their own vocabulary to talk about issues.  That vocabulary is based on their own implementations.   They use function and field names that you are likely not familiar with. 

Don't gloss over this.  Ask for explanations in plain language.  Get the agent to talk YOUR language and explain their language so that you can create the right mental model for what is going on.

I recently had a rather protracted discussion with @grok about an issue that it had raised that I couldn't make sense of.  After several Q&A iterations I realized that it had conflated two similar issues into one and was using language that did not disambiguate them.  Once I realized this I was able to point it out to grok. It had an "AHA" moment and realized that there were two issues instead of one; and it broke through the conflation.   We were both suddenly on the same page.

Amazing!

results.text:
I put up a new morning bathrobe rant. Then I told my Grok Bot that I had posted it. And that it should be on my website. It did the rest. it opened up the GitHub repository for my website, it changed the code to put a link to the video on it. Then it deployed. All while I was sitting on my porch, reading the news.

This is the way everything is going to be — If we allow it — If we build the data centers. And we should. Because this is the way it should be.

I like having machines take care of the rote boring nonsense. You should too.

results.text:
Have you noticed that when you call businesses an AI sometimes answers? I called a plumber recently and “Rudy“ answered. Rudy was so friendly and effusive that I immediately suspected that it was an AI. So I asked it, point blank, are you an AI? Rudy answered “yes I’m your helpful AI assistant”. Then it and I had an extremely efficient, very pleasant, conversation about what I needed. It knew all the facts, had the schedule right there, I got an appointment confirmed within 90 seconds. 

I was not put on hold, I was not subjected to someone who could not speak the language, I was not subjected to someone who is so new to their job that they didn’t know how to find the keys on the keyboard. It was a remarkably good experience.

Soon, everything is going to be like that. No more “Press one for…”.
